title: 2D Pocket offset rings: waterline-like passes with a nominal engagement, not a constant-engagement spiral

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
## What happens

In a 2D Pocket, the Passes tab "Offset rings" strategy does not cut the way a user expects from an adaptive strategy.

- It behaves like a waterline pass with an engagement setting.
- It is not a spiral with a constant engagement that goes outward.

The maintainer reported this. He set the priority at `P2`.

## What is expected

The offset rings strategy is an adaptive strategy:

- It walks outward in a spiral.
- The engagement stays constant along the pass. The step and the loop width come from the engagement limit.
- The tool does not repeat the waterline shape of the pocket.

## Why it matters

- The user chooses "Offset rings" to control the tool load. A waterline pass with a nominal engagement does not do that.
- The difference changes the tool life, the surface and the cut time.

## What to check

- The ring planner of the 2D Pocket Offset rings strategy: does it read the engagement limit at each level, or only once?
- The relation with #3932 (2D Adaptive trochoidal: slots to a wall, no outside start). Both report that an adaptive name gives a non-adaptive path.
- The pins: the `pocket_*` suites and the example catalog cases may assert the waterline shape as correct.

## Missing at filing

- The sketch, the tool, the stock and the posted program. Add them as a comment when the case is reproduced.

If a pass can gouge the part or a fixture, raise this issue to `P1`.
